I have conducted an academic literature survey on 'AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Cloud-Based APIs'. Here are some key findings from the research papers I found:

1. **CloudAnoAgent**: This paper proposes the first neuro-symbolic Large Language Model (LLM)-based agent for anomaly detection in cloud environments. It integrates LLMs with log data to enable more accurate and interpretable anomaly detection.

2. **Cloud Platform Network Traffic Monitoring**: This study introduces an LLM-based network traffic monitoring and anomaly detection system for cloud platforms. It addresses the rapidly evolving nature of cloud platforms and the growing complexity of network traffic, ensuring network security and performance.

3. **End-to-End Anomaly Detection in Cloud Control Plane**: This paper demonstrates an end-to-end anomaly detection pipeline for detecting performance problems in cloud control planes. It integrates a data pipeline with a machine learning-driven anomaly detection engine, catering to the needs of a large-scale cloud control plane.

4. **AI-driven Anomaly Detection in Cloud Computing Environments**: This review explores AI-driven approaches to anomaly detection in cloud computing environments. It discusses the applications of various AI techniques in enhancing cloud security, optimizing performance, and ensuring efficient resource management.

5. **AI-Driven Anomaly Detection for Secure Identity and Access Management**: This paper examines the limitations of traditional machine learning and basic artificial neural networks in detecting complex anomalies. It highlights the need for more efficient and accurate anomaly detection technologies for secure identity and access management in cloud computing.

These papers provide a good starting point for further research into AI-driven anomaly detection for cloud-based APIs.
